display.name: Client Metrics
display.description: Per-client SDK metrics from @dxos/observability. Gauges are read at collection time and exported every 60s, so every panel aggregates ACROSS clients: avg/p90/max answer "what does a typical or bad client look like", sum answers "how much is out there in total". ctx.tag isolates a single local run from deployed traffic.

display.name: deployment.environment
display.description: Deployment environment; local runs report 'unknown' unless DX_ENVIRONMENT is set.

display.name: ctx.tag
display.description: Client tag from DX_TELEMETRY_TAG; use it to isolate one run.

display.name: Documents loaded per client (avg)
display.description: location=local — the resident document count.

filter.expression: deployment.environment in $deployment.environment AND ctx.tag in $ctx.tag AND location = 'local'

display.name: Unsynced documents (fleet total)
display.description: Summed across clients — total outstanding backlog.

display.name: Heap pressure (worst client %)
display.description: heapUsed / heapSizeLimit. Above ~90% the browser is close to an OOM kill.

display.name: Spaces per client — avg / max
display.description: Aggregated across clients within each bucket. No p90/p99: SigNoz only supports percentile space aggregation on histograms, not gauges.

display.name: Known vs ready spaces (avg per client)
display.description: The gap is spaces the client knows about but has not opened.

display.name: Documents per client by location
display.description: local vs remote; they converge when the client is fully synced.

display.name: Unsynced backlog per client — avg / max
display.description: p90/p99 would need this exported as a histogram; a gauge only supports avg/min/max/sum across clients. A max that stays flat while avg sits near 0 is still a single stuck client.

display.name: Heap used — avg / max
display.description: Thresholds mark the 300-400MB resting target from the memory-usage project. Percentiles across clients need a histogram; a gauge cannot provide them.

display.name: Time to sync — min / avg / max
display.description: Duration of each completed sync episode, merged across clients. A client that never finishes syncing contributes nothing here — see the stall panel.

display.name: Time without sync progress — avg / max
display.description: Age of the last decrease in the backlog while a client is not caught up; 0 when caught up. This is the stuck detector: >600s means a client has made no progress for ten minutes.

display.name: Event loop lag — main thread
display.description: Peak time a timer fired behind schedule per window, i.e. how long the tab was blocked. Main thread lag is felt directly as UI jank.

filter.expression: deployment.environment in $deployment.environment AND ctx.tag in $ctx.tag AND dxos.process.type = 'browser'
deployment.environment in $deployment.environment AND ctx.tag in $ctx.tag AND dxos.process.type = 'browser'

display.name: Event loop lag — workers
display.description: Same measure inside the shared and dedicated workers, where client-services runs. Worker lag does not jank the UI directly; it shows up as RPC queue wait on the panel below.

filter.expression: deployment.environment in $deployment.environment AND ctx.tag in $ctx.tag AND dxos.process.type in ('shared-worker', 'dedicated-worker', 'service-worker')
deployment.environment in $deployment.environment AND ctx.tag in $ctx.tag AND dxos.process.type in ('shared-worker', 'dedicated-worker', 'service-worker')

display.name: RPC queue wait vs service time — max
display.description: Queue wait is time the message spent waiting for the thread; service time is time spent working. Queue wait rising while service time is flat means the receiving realm is saturated, not slow.

display.name: EDGE reconnects by cause
display.description: offline = the browser reported no network; abnormal = closed with no close frame while online; server_error/going_away = the server closed deliberately; inactivity_timeout = the peer went silent while our pings were flowing.

display.name: Reconnects per session — avg / max
display.description: Counted since the process started, so the value IS the per-session total; it resets on reload. A delta counter cannot answer this.

display.name: Fleet connectivity
display.description: Average of a 0/1 gauge, so this is the fraction of clients with an open EDGE socket.

display.name: Pending sync work per client — avg / max
display.description: Documents plus feed blocks — the same definition the episode and stall instruments use, so this panel and the stall alert agree.

display.name: Heaviest clients by heap
display.description: One row per device; heapSizeLimit is the browser's cap for that client.
